answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the island index resolves every citation against the vertex checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the walnut audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 173 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 173 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 35 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
